security: This endpoint grants arbitrary PowerShell exec as the remote user, with no sandbox. The file tools (read_file/write_file/file_hash) ARE confined to C:\BHH\MCP-Server: absolute paths and ../ traversal that leave the root are rejected with 'path escapes root', and reading a directory returns EISDIR. The pairing code is still equivalent to full host control - via exec, not via the file tools. Treat it as a secret.

security_correction.retracted: unrestricted file read/write as the remote user
evidence: write_file C:/Windows/Temp/escape-abs.txt -> Error: path escapes root: C:/Windows/Temp/escape-abs.txt
write_file perf-test/rw/../../../escape2.txt -> Error: path escapes root: perf-test/rw/../../../escape2.txt
read_file C:/Windows/System32/drivers/etc/hosts -> Error: path escapes root: C:/Windows/System32/drivers/etc/hosts
file_hash perf-test/rw -> Error: EISDIR: illegal operation on a directory, read
write_file perf-test/rw/../../escape-attempt.txt -> normalized back inside the root, NOT an escape
security_correction.still_true: the pairing code grants full host control through exec

file_tool_capabilities.write_file: byte-exact for ASCII, LF/CRLF/mixed newlines, multi-byte UTF-8 + emoji, empty content, no-trailing-newline; preserves a UTF-8 BOM; auto-creates missing parent directories
file_tool_capabilities.expectedHash: real compare-and-swap precondition: stale -> 'Error: stale-file: expected <hash>, got <hash>' with the file untouched; a missing path is treated as empty content (atomic create-if-absent); under contention exactly one writer wins
file_tool_capabilities.read_file: line-paged (0-based offset, limit <= 2000, totalLines, truncated); returns content byte-identically for text; newlines are NOT normalized; binary content is lossily decoded (text-only channel)
file_tool_capabilities.file_hash: sha256 + bytes; agrees with PowerShell Get-FileHash; ENOENT for a missing path, EISDIR for a directory
file_tool_capabilities.bom_note: read content may begin with U+FEFF; no byte view is available through read_file, so use file_hash when bytes matter
